objects.description: Strongly-typed enum of JWT/JWKS verification statuses used throughout the library to report success (Ok) or the first error encountered during parsing/validation. Values cover JWT structure, header/payload parsing, signature issues, and JWKS/PEM/X509 problems.

Base utility class that tracks an internal Status representing OK or the first failure encountered. Provides getStatus(), protected updateStatus() to latch the first non-OK status, and resetStatus() to set the current status. Designed to be inherited by components performing JWT/JWKS operations.

Utility class to read typed values from a google::protobuf::Struct representing JSON-like data. Provides methods to retrieve strings, unsigned 64-bit integers, doubles, booleans, string lists (e.g., JWT "aud"), and to find nested values. Holds a const reference to the source Struct; it does not own or modify it. Construction requires an existing Struct. Destruction has no special requirements. Thread-safety depends on external synchronization of the referenced Struct.

Enumeration of result codes returned by StructUtils getters: OK for success; MISSING when the named field is not present; WRONG_TYPE when the JSON value exists but is of an unexpected type; OUT_OF_RANGE when a numeric conversion exceeds allowed bounds (e.g., positive uint64 range). This enum is a nested type within StructUtils.

A utility class to validate JWT audience claims against a configured set. It normalizes audience URIs by removing the scheme and trailing slash before comparison. Construct with a list of allowed audiences, query with areAudiencesAllowed, and check emptiness with empty. Ownership and lifecycle are standard C++ object semantics; no special destruction requirements beyond RAII are indicated.
Alias for a std::unique_ptr managing a CheckAudience instance, providing exclusive ownership semantics. Use to dynamically allocate and manage CheckAudience without manual delete.

A concrete struct that models a parsed JSON Web Token (JWT), storing the original token, decoded header and payload in both string and google::protobuf::Struct forms, signature, standard claims (alg, kid, iss, sub, aud, iat, nbf, exp, jti), and providing parsing and time-constraint verification helpers. Copying is explicit and non-trivial. Construction/destruction are standard; no custom allocator or ownership rules are declared.

Holds and parses a JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) or PEM-formatted keys for JWT verification. Provides factory methods to build a key set from JWKS or PEM input, and an API to add a PEM key. Inherits WithStatus for construction/parse status reporting. Owns a vector of Pubkey objects representing individual keys.
Enumeration inside Jwks specifying the input format for creating a Jwks: JWKS (JSON Web Key Set) or PEM.

Represents a single JSON Web Key. Holds key material and metadata: HMAC secret (hmac_key_), key ID (kid_), key type (kty_), algorithm (alg_), curve (crv_), and parsed OpenSSL handles for RSA, EC, OKP raw key bytes, BIO/X509 as applicable. Memory is managed via bssl::UniquePtr. Fields are optional depending on key type.
Alias for a unique_ptr managing a Jwks instance. Use to hold ownership of a parsed key set.

Status is referenced as the return type of verification functions but is not defined in this header. It is likely an enum or class representing success/failure and error reasons, defined in jwt_verify_lib/status.h. No definition is present here.

Jwt represents a parsed JSON Web Token object used as input to verification. It is referenced via const reference parameters but defined elsewhere (jwt_verify_lib/jwt.h). No definition is present here.
Jwks represents a JSON Web Key Set used to verify JWT signatures. It is referenced via const reference parameters but defined elsewhere (jwt_verify_lib/jwks.h). No definition is present here.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets the fuzzer stubs that build a google::protobuf::Struct and
# subsequently query fields by top-level names produced via FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# The stubs sanitize names by replacing dots and non [A-Za-z0-9_] with underscores
# and may truncate base keys to 32 chars. They also use a separate unsigned int seed
# (via FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)) to decide how many fields (1..5) to create and their kinds.
#
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR is used for:
# - key_base when constructing the Struct (sanitized to [A-Za-z0-9_], max 32)
# - field names for lookups in GetString/GetUInt64/GetDouble/GetBoolean/GetStringList
#   (dots replaced with underscores). If the lookup name matches one of the generated
#   keys, getters can successfully extract values.
#
# Therefore, we craft an input buffer that encodes:
# 1) The unsigned int seed (4 bytes, little-endian) used by the constructor stub to
#    select field count and per-field kind deterministically.
# 2) A key_base string (alphanumeric + underscore), up to 32 bytes (the stub truncates longer).
#    The constructor creates keys: key_base_0, key_base_1, ...
# 3) A sequence of candidate query names for later FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls so that some
#    queries will hit existing keys (to exercise OK paths) while others may miss or hit
#    type-mismatches (to exercise non-OK paths). We include exact top-level keys as well
#    as unrelated names. Each string is length-prefixed to be decoded by the fuzzing
#    harness' string provider (common pattern). Since the exact FUZZ framework is opaque,
#    we provide a flat bytes buffer with ASCII segments separated by newlines as well,
#    which many fuzzers use to split parameters. This keeps inputs valid and simple.
#
# Format we output (human-readable, newline-separated tokens):
# - First line: SEED=<uint>
# - Second line: KEYBASE=<sanitized>
# - Following lines: names to be consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR in subsequent stubs, including
#   the generated keys (KEYBASE_0..KEYBASE_4), some variant names, and common claim-like keys.
#
# The harness will likely just pull bytes sequentially; even if it ignores the labels,
# it will still see a sequence of alphanumeric strings separated by newlines, which
# satisfies FUZZ_PARAM_STR expectations and improves chance of matching keys.

ALNUM_US = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"


def _rand_keybase(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 4, max_len: int = 24) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Ensure it starts with a letter to be tidy, then fill with allowed chars.
    first = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters)
    rest = ''.join(rng.choice(ALNUM_US) for _ in range(n - 1))
    return (first + rest)[:32]


def _gen_query_names(key_base: str, seed: int) -> List[str]:
    names = []
    # Exact keys likely present: key_base_0..key_base_4 (constructor makes 1..5 fields)
    for i in range(5):
        names.append(f"{key_base}_{i}")
    # Some likely string-list nested-looking names (dots will be sanitized to underscores in stubs)
    names.extend([
        key_base,  # base alone (likely missing)
        f"{key_base}_aud",  # could be treated as audience-like list
        f"{key_base}_flag",  # could be boolean
        f"{key_base}_num",   # could be numeric
        f"{key_base}_child", # subkey possibly inside nested struct (top-level miss)
    ])
    # Common claim-like names to exercise WRONG_TYPE/MISSING branches when present/absent.
    names.extend([
        "iss", "sub", "aud", "iat", "nbf", "exp", "jti",
        "count", "enabled", "ratio",
    ])
    # Include some variations with different cases and underscores
    names.extend([
        key_base.upper() + "_0",
        key_base.lower() + "_1",
        key_base.capitalize() + "_2",
    ])
    # De-duplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq = []
    for n in names:
        if n not in seen:
            uniq.append(n)
            seen.add(n)
    # Add a few random filler names
    rng = random.Random(seed ^ 0x9E3779B1)
    for _ in range(10):
        ln = rng.randint(3, 16)
        uniq.append(''.join(rng.choice(ALNUM_US) for _ in range(ln)))
    return uniq


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # 1) Choose a deterministic 32-bit seed value for the C++ constructor stub
    seed_u32 = rng.getrandbits(32)
    # 2) Build key_base within allowed chars
    key_base = _rand_keybase(rng)
    # 3) Build query names list
    queries = _gen_query_names(key_base, seed_u32)

    # Assemble a simple text buffer. Newline-separated tokens are friendly to many FUZZ_PARAM_STR providers.
    lines = []
    lines.append(f"SEED={seed_u32}")
    lines.append(f"KEYBASE={key_base}")
    # Include the exact keys first to maximize chances early calls succeed
    lines.extend(queries)

    # Join and ensure total size <= 4096 bytes
    blob = ('\n'.join(lines)).encode('ascii', 'ignore')
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        blob = blob[:4096]
    return blob

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces a short ASCII string that the fuzzer stub will
# sanitize to [A-Za-z0-9_] and then insert up to two dots to make a nested path.
# We therefore provide strings that already contain reasonable field-name tokens
# separated by dots or underscores so that after sanitization and dot insertion
# they remain meaningful. We vary length and composition to exercise edge cases
# like short names, long-ish names, and multiple segments.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"

# Common field-name tokens to increase chance of matching real data
TOKENS = [
    "iss", "sub", "aud", "exp", "nbf", "iat", "jti",
    "header", "payload", "signature", "alg", "kid", "typ",
    "x5c", "x5t", "crv", "kty", "n", "e", "x", "y",
    # generic names
    "a", "b", "c", "user", "name", "id", "roles", "scopes",
    "nested", "config", "jwks", "keys", "values", "meta",
]

def _rand_token(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 12) -> str:
    # Bias toward known tokens, otherwise synthesize
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return rng.choice(TOKENS)
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(length))

def _compose_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build 1-4 segments joined by either dot or underscore
    segments: List[str] = []
    count = rng.choices([1, 2, 3, 4], weights=[2, 4, 3, 1], k=1)[0]
    for _ in range(count):
        tok = _rand_token(rng)
        # Occasionally add a numeric suffix to test numeric field names
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            tok += str(rng.randint(0, 999))
        segments.append(tok)
    sep = rng.choice(['.', '_'])
    base = sep.join(segments)

    # Occasionally pad with extra valid chars to make string long enough for stub to insert dots
    if len(base) < 8 and rng.random() < 0.5:
        pad = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 8)))
        # prepend or append
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            base = pad + base
        else:
            base = base + pad

    # Ensure length not excessive
    return base[:64]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Produce a set of candidate paths and pick one to return to add variability
    candidates = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 5)):
        candidates.append(_compose_path(rng))

    s = rng.choice(candidates)
    # The stub will sanitize to alnum/underscore and insert dots; keep within 4096 bytes
    return s.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: URL or audience string
# We want to generate bytes that, when consumed by the fuzzer as FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int),
# yield interesting, yet valid audience/URL-like strings. The buffer should contain multiple strings and some
# integral values the harness will read. We will pack them as length-prefixed UTF-8 strings followed by
# some 32-bit unsigned integers. The fuzzing harness typically slices the input sequentially for FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# calls; length-prefixing helps ensure each call gets a coherent value.
#
# The target stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR up to 7 times total (s1, s2, s3 in ctor; a1..a4 in areAudiencesAllowed),
# and FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) twice (for counts). We'll generate:
# - 8 strings to have extra variety
# - 4 unsigned ints
# The fuzzer runtime will likely just consume sequentially; extra data is fine.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

SCHEMES = ["http://", "https://", "HTTP://", "HTTPS://", "hTtPs://"]
HOST_TOKENS = [
    "service", "api", "auth", "login", "user", "accounts", "data", "v1", "v2", "static",
    "cdn", "files", "upload", "download", "oauth", "openid", "jwt", "verify", "example",
]
TLDS = ["com", "org", "net", "io", "dev", "local", "example"]
PATH_SEGS = [
    "", "", "",  # bias towards shallow paths
    "", "health", "metrics", "token", "callback", "foo", "bar", "baz", "v1", "v2", "users",
    "profile", "resources", "graphql", "rest", "rpc"
]

# Some pre-crafted interesting audiences to mix in
INTERESTING_AUDS = [
    "service", "SERVICE", "api", "api/", "api:read", "urn:service", "aud", "aud/", "", 
    "example.com", "EXAMPLE.com", 
    # With scheme and trailing slash variants
    "https://service/", "http://service", "HTTPS://EXAMPLE.COM/", 
    # With ports and paths
    "https://example.com:443/", "http://localhost:8080", "https://api.example.io/v1/",
]


def _rand_host(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a host like sub.domain.tld with optional hyphens and digits
    parts = []
    nlabels = r.randint(1, 3)
    for _ in range(nlabels):
        base = r.choice(HOST_TOKENS)
        # optional decoration
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            base += "-" + r.choice(HOST_TOKENS)
        if r.random() < 0.2:
            base += str(r.randint(0, 999))
        # maybe uppercase some
        if r.random() < 0.15:
            base = base.upper()
        parts.append(base)
    tld = r.choice(TLDS)
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        tld = tld.upper()
    return ".".join(parts + [tld])


def _rand_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    segs: List[str] = []
    n = r.randint(0, 3)
    for _ in range(n):
        seg = r.choice(PATH_SEGS)
        if seg == "":
            continue
        # occasionally add id-like piece
        if r.random() < 0.2:
            seg += "/" + str(r.randint(1, 9999))
        segs.append(seg)
    return ("/" + "/".join(segs)) if segs else ("/" if r.random() < 0.3 else "")


def _rand_query(r: random.Random) -> str:
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        k = r.choice(["aud", "scope", "q", "id"]) \
            + "=" + r.choice(["read", "write", "all", "1"])
        return "?" + k
    return ""


def gen_audience_like(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate either a bare audience token or a URL-like audience
    choice = r.random()
    if choice < 0.25:
        return r.choice(INTERESTING_AUDS)
    if choice < 0.55:
        # Bare token
        token_parts = []
        n = r.randint(1, 3)
        for _ in range(n):
            s = r.choice(HOST_TOKENS)
            if r.random() < 0.3:
                s = s.upper()
            token_parts.append(s)
        base = ":".join(token_parts) if r.random() < 0.2 else "".join(token_parts)
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            base += "/"
        return base
    # URL-like
    scheme = r.choice(SCHEMES) if r.random() < 0.9 else ""
    host = _rand_host(r)
    # optional port
    port = ":" + str(r.choice([80, 443, r.randint(1, 65535)])) if r.random() < 0.25 else ""
    path = _rand_path(r)
    query = _rand_query(r)
    aud = f"{scheme}{host}{port}{path}{query}"
    # Occasionally add trailing slash explicitly to exercise normalization
    if r.random() < 0.4 and not aud.endswith("/") and query == "":
        aud += "/"
    return aud


def pack_len_prefixed_strings(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Each string encoded as: 2-byte big-endian length, then bytes (UTF-8), truncated to 512
    out = bytearray()
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8')[:512]
        l = len(b)
        out.append((l >> 8) & 0xFF)
        out.append(l & 0xFF)
        out.extend(b)
    return bytes(out)


def pack_u32(values: List[int]) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for v in values:
        v &= 0xFFFFFFFF
        out.extend([(v >> 24) & 0xFF, (v >> 16) & 0xFF, (v >> 8) & 0xFF, v & 0xFF])
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Generate a pool of audience-like strings.
    strings: List[str] = []
    # Ensure entries that will likely match after normalization by pairing scheme/no-scheme and trailing slash
    base_match = gen_audience_like(r)
    norm_no_scheme = base_match
    # Create variants
    if not base_match.startswith("http"):
        # add scheme variant
        scheme_variant = r.choice(["http://", "https://"]) + base_match.strip("/") + "/"
    else:
        # remove scheme
        without = base_match
        for sch in ["http://", "https://", "HTTP://", "HTTPS://"]:
            if without.startswith(sch):
                without = without[len(sch):]
                break
        scheme_variant = without.rstrip("/")
    strings.append(base_match)
    strings.append(scheme_variant)

    # Add additional random strings to reach at least 8
    while len(strings) < 8:
        s = gen_audience_like(r)
        strings.append(s)

    # Build unsigned ints to control counts in stubs: values 0..3 and 0..4 distributions
    u_count_ctor = r.randint(0, 3)
    u_count_call = r.randint(0, 4)
    # Add some extras for potential future consumers
    extra1 = r.getrandbits(32)
    extra2 = r.getrandbits(32)

    blob = bytearray()
    blob.extend(pack_len_prefixed_strings(strings))
    blob.extend(pack_u32([u_count_ctor, u_count_call, extra1, extra2]))

    # Ensure size limit
    return bytes(blob[:MAX_TOTAL])

import base64
import json
import random
import time
from typing import Dict, Any, List

# Utilities for base64url without padding

def b64url_nopad(data: bytes) -> str:
    s = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(data).decode('ascii')
    return s.rstrip('=')

# Build JWT header/payload/signature with valid base64url compact form.
# Focus on producing syntactically valid tokens that exercise different parsing paths in parseFromString.

ALG_CHOICES = [
    # Common algorithms supported by many JWT libs
    "HS256", "HS384", "HS512",
    "RS256", "RS384", "RS512",
    "ES256", "ES384", "ES512",
    # OKP/EdDSA
    "EdDSA",
]

# Some plausible kids
KID_PREFIXES = ["kid", "key", "id", ""]

# Audience variants to exercise string and array handling
AUDIENCE_SETS: List[Any] = [
    # Single string
    "api",
    "https://service/",
    "http://example.com/resource",
    # Array
    ["api"],
    ["one", "two"],
    ["https://svc", "svc"],
]

SUB_CHOICES = ["test", "user", "alice", "bob", "", "123"]
ISS_CHOICES = [
    "issuer", "https://issuer.example.com/", "http://i/", "urn:foo:bar", "me"
]
JTI_CHOICES = ["jti1", "token-id", "abc", ""]

# Deterministic pseudo-random signature bytes; for HMAC/none-like we just fill bytes.
# The library under test will validate signature later; here we only need base64url bytes.

def make_signature(rng: random.Random, alg: str) -> bytes:
    # Choose lengths to cover different paths (including Ed25519 length expectation)
    if alg == "EdDSA":
        # Ed25519 signatures are 64 bytes; produce 64 to hit happy path, or others to hit length checks downstream
        length = rng.choice([64, 32, 48, 80])
    elif alg.startswith("ES"):
        # ECDSA DER varies; but parser only base64url-decodes at this stage; pick a range
        length = rng.choice([64, 70, 72, 96])
    elif alg.startswith("RS"):
        length = rng.choice([64, 128, 256])
    else:
        # HMAC lengths arbitrary
        length = rng.choice([16, 32, 48, 64])
    return rng.randbytes(length)

# Construct header JSON with typical fields, sometimes adding extra fields.

def make_header(rng: random.Random) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    hdr: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    alg = rng.choice(ALG_CHOICES)
    hdr["alg"] = alg
    # 50% chance include kid
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        prefix = rng.choice(KID_PREFIXES)
        suffix = str(rng.randint(1, 999)) if prefix else str(rng.randint(1, 9999))
        kid = (prefix + ("-" if prefix and rng.random() < 0.7 else "") + suffix).strip("-")
        hdr["kid"] = kid
    # Occasionally add typ or cty
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        hdr["typ"] = rng.choice(["JWT", "JOSE", "application/jwt"])
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        hdr["cty"] = rng.choice(["JWT", "application/json", ""])
    # Extra header param to exercise parsing
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        hdr["crit"] = rng.sample(["exp", "nbf", "aud"], k=rng.randint(1, 3))
    return hdr

# Construct payload JSON with standard claims and variant types/values within validity bounds

def make_payload(rng: random.Random) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    now = int(time.time())
    skew = 60
    pl: Dict[str, Any] = {}

    # iss/sub optional
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        pl["iss"] = rng.choice(ISS_CHOICES)
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        pl["sub"] = rng.choice(SUB_CHOICES)

    # iat/nbf/exp set to valid ranges relative to now
    base_iat = now - rng.randint(0, 3600)
    pl["iat"] = base_iat
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        pl["nbf"] = base_iat - rng.randint(0, skew)
    # ensure exp >= iat typically
    lifetime = rng.randint(30, 24 * 3600)
    pl["exp"] = base_iat + lifetime

    # jti optional
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        pl["jti"] = rng.choice(JTI_CHOICES)

    # Audience: sometimes string, sometimes array
    if rng.random() < 0.9:
        aud_choice = rng.choice(AUDIENCE_SETS)
        pl["aud"] = aud_choice

    # Add some custom claims of varying types
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        pl["scope"] = rng.choice(["read", "read write", "*"])
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        pl["admin"] = rng.choice([True, False])
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        pl["rate"] = round(rng.uniform(0.0, 1000.0), 3)
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        pl["nested"] = {"a": {"b": rng.randint(0, 10)}}

    return pl

# Serialize JSON deterministically (no whitespace) for compact base64url

def json_compact(obj: Dict[str, Any]) -> bytes:
    return json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")

# Build a valid compact JWT string

def make_jwt_compact(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    hdr = make_header(rng)
    alg = hdr.get("alg", "HS256")
    pl = make_payload(rng)

    hdr_b64 = b64url_nopad(json_compact(hdr))
    pl_b64 = b64url_nopad(json_compact(pl))

    sig_bytes = make_signature(rng, alg)
    sig_b64 = b64url_nopad(sig_bytes)

    return f"{hdr_b64}.{pl_b64}.{sig_b64}"

# Sometimes return a minimal syntactically valid token similar to the stub fallback

def make_minimal_token() -> str:
    hdr = b64url_nopad(b'{"alg":"HS256"}')
    pl = b64url_nopad(b'{"sub":"test","iat":1}')
    sig = "AA"
    return f"{hdr}.{pl}.{sig}"

# Public API

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # With some probability, emit the minimal fixed token used in the fuzzer stub to make sure paths match
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        token = make_minimal_token()
    else:
        token = make_jwt_compact(rng)

    # Return as bytes; limit size to <= 4096 (these tokens are small)
    data = token.encode("ascii")
    if len(data) > 4096:
        # Extremely unlikely; truncate signature segment to fit while keeping three-part structure
        parts = token.split('.')
        if len(parts) == 3:
            max_sig_len = max(1, 4096 - (len(parts[0]) + len(parts[1]) + 2))
            parts[2] = parts[2][:max_sig_len]
            data = (parts[0] + '.' + parts[1] + '.' + parts[2]).encode('ascii')
        else:
            data = data[:4096]
    return data
